questions.question: Who among the following was the court poet of Harshavardhana and the author of ‘Harshacharita’?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__ Banabhatta.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Banabhatta was the court poet of king Harshavardhana.
 
• Banabhatta wrote Harshvardhan's biography Harshacharita in Sanskrit.
 
• He describes his association with Thanesar in his biography.

About Banabhatta:__

__
 
• A great poet of India, Banabhatta was born around the** 7th century in a village in India.**
 
• He was born in Pritikuta village, which was situated on the banks of Hiranyavahu.
 
• He was born to Chitrabhanu and Rajadevi and he was a family of Vatsyayana gotra.
 
• This poetic genius wrote one of the most famous and earliest novels,** known as Kadambari.**
 
• It is a biographical work of** Harsha and Kadambari.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• ** Rajashekhara was a Sanskrit poet** and playwright who lived in the 9th century CE.

 
 
• He is known for his works such as Karpuramanjari and Bala Ramayana, but he was not a court poet of Harshavardhana.
 
 
 
• **Kalidas was a renowned poet and dramatist **who lived in ancient India, probably in the 4th or 5th century CE.
 
 
• He is known for his works such as Abhijnanasakuntalam, Meghadutam, and Raghuvamsa, but he was not a court poet of Harshavardhana.
 
 
 
• **Aryabhatta was a mathematician and astronomer **who lived in ancient India, probably in the 5th or 6th century CE.
 
 
• He is known for his contributions to the fields of mathematics, astronomy, and astrology, but he was not a court poet of Harshavardhana.

questions.question: How many points advantage must a freestyle wrestler must have against his/ her opponent for the bout to be declared over?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** 10.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **In freestyle wrestling, if one wrestler has a 10-point advantage over their opponent, the bout is declared over and the wrestler with the advantage wins by technical superiority.**
 
• This rule is in place to prevent a wrestler from being excessively beaten or injured in a match.

**Wrestling: **__

__
 
• Wrestling is a hand-to-hand combat system.
 
• It is a set of combat sports involving grappling-type techniques such as clinch fighting, throws and takedowns, joint locks, pins, and other grappling holds.
 
• Wrestling techniques have been incorporated into martial arts, combat sports, and military systems.

​Wrestling duration:__

__
 
• A typical freestyle wrestling bout, much like Greco-Roman, is divided into two periods of three minutes each with a 30-second break in between.
 
• For official Under-15, cadets, and veteran competitions, the periods are curtailed to two minutes each.
 
• Two competing wrestlers face each other on a mat, nine-meter in diameter, with the primary objective of pinning the opponent’s shoulders to the mat for a short duration of time, which hands the wrestler an instant victory by ‘fall’.
 
• 
 
Thus, two periods of three minutes is correct with reference to a wrestling match.__

 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] __Additional Information:__

 
Wrestling in the Olympics:

 
 
• The International Olympic Committee (IOC) was formed, and the first Games were planned for 1896 in Athens, the capital of Greece.
 
• In Athens, 280 participants from 13 nations competed in 43 events, covering track-and-field, swimming, gymnastics, cycling, wrestling, weightlifting, fencing, shooting, and tennis.
 
• Since the Olympic Games began in Athens in 1896, wrestling (in the form of Greco-Roman wrestling) became a focus of the Games, with the exception of the 1900 Summer Olympics when wrestling did not appear on the program.
 
• Freestyle wrestling and weight classes both made their first appearance in 1904.

questions.question: In India Green Revolution was led by :

• The Green Revolution is referred to as a period when Indian agriculture was converted to an industrial system due to the adoption of modern methods and technologies.
 
• It included the use of products like High-Yielding variety seeds, tractors, irrigation facilities, pesticides, and fertilizers which were not used or used very limitedly.
 
• Indian agriculture made a transition from old manual methods to new, innovative, and technological methods.
 
• The movement of the green revolution was a great success that changed the country's status from a food-deficient economy to one of the world's leading agricultural nations.
 
• This revolution led to an increase in food grain production, in Punjab, Haryana, and Uttar Pradesh.

questions.question: Which of the following is known as the Flying Sikh of India?
questions.solution:
__Milkha Singh__ was called the ‘Flying Sikh’.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• He is a former Indian track and field sprinter who had been introduced to the sport while serving in the Indian Army.
 
• He was the only Indian athlete to win an individual athletics gold medal at a Commonwealth Games until Krishna Poonia at the 2010 Commonwealth Games won the gold medal for the discus.
 
• In recognition of his sporting achievements, he was awarded the Padma Shri, India's fourth-highest civilian honor.
 
• He represented India at the Melbourne Summer Olympics of 1956, at the Rome Summer Olympics of 1960 and at the Tokyo Summer Olympics of 1964.
 
• He was a former Indian track and field sprinter.
 
• He won Gold Medal in 1958 and 1962 Asian Games.
 
• He finished at 4th place in the 1960 Rome Olympic.
 
• He was awarded Padma Shree for his contribution to the sport.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The "Flying Sikh" nickname he acquired from General Ayub Khan of Pakistan after defeating Abdul Khaliq in Pakistan in 1960.

 
 
• Milkha Singh is the first person from India to win a Gold medal in Individual athletics at the Commonwealth Games. 
 
• He also won two gold medals in the Asian Games in 1958 and 1962.
 
• He has represented India in the three Summer Olympics such as the one in 1956 at Melbourne respectively in 1960 at Rome and in 1964 at Tokyo.
 
 
• The Indian government has honoured him by awarding the fourth-highest civilian award Padma Shri for his achievements in sports.
 
 
 
• Milkha won over Abdul Khaliq, the Pakistani Athlete in **1960** during the 200m event at an **International Athletic competition in Lahore**.
 
• The then General Ayub Khan, commented post-race stating him as **"Flying Sikh"**.

questions.question: What was the approximate percentage contribution of the industrial sector to GDP in 1950-51?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**11.8.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• The industrial sector contributed approximately 11.8% to India's GDP in 1950-51.
 
• This was a significant increase from the pre-independence period where the contribution was only around 6%.
 
• The industrial sector played a crucial role in the economic development of India post-independence.
 
• The growth of industries led to the creation of employment opportunities, which further boosted the economy.
 
• The industrial policy that India developed was closely tied to trade law.
 
• Trade was characterized in the first seven plans by what is referred to as an internal trading strategy.
 
• This tactic is known as import substitution technically.
 
• This approach attempted to supplement indigenous production with imports.
 
• The government shielded indigenous industries from foreign competition under this policy.
 
• Two methods were used to prevent imports: tariffs, and quotas.
 
• Tariffs are a charge on imported goods; they raise the cost of imports and reduce demand for them.
 
• The amount of merchandise that may be imported is determined by quotas.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• The Economic Survey document is prepared by the Economics Division of the Department of Economic Affairs (DEA) under the guidance of the Chief Economic Advisor.
 
• It is usually presented a day before the Union Budget is presented in Parliament.
 
• The first Economic Survey in India was presented in the year 1950- 51.
 
• Up to 1964, it was presented along with the Union Budget. From 1964 onwards, it has been delinked from the Budget.

questions.question: What is the atomic mass of Nitrogen?
questions.solution:

• The atomic mass of nitrogen is 14 µ. 
 
• 
 Atom: 

 
 
• An atom is the smallest invisible unit of matter that constitutes a chemical element.
 
• Every plasma, solid, gas & liquid, is composed of ionized or neutral atoms.
 
• Around 100 picometers across, atoms are extremely small. 
 
 
 
• Atomic Mass: 
 
 
• The Atomic Theory of Dalton suggested that each element has a unique atomic mass.
 
• The law of constant proportions could be explained easily by the implementation of Dalton's theory.
 
• As the size of an atom is relatively small, it is quite difficult to determine the mass of an atom.
 
• That's why scientists started evaluating the mass of an atom by differentiating it from the mass of a standard atom.
 
• The atomic mass is 12u (12 atomic mass units).
 
• Thus it states that 1 atomic mass unit = Mass of 1/12 the mass of a carbon-12 atom.

questions.question: Which article of the Indian Constitution states that India is a ‘Union of States'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article1.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• According to Article 1, the territory of India can be classified into three categories:

 
 
• Territories of the states
 
• Union territories
 
• Territories that may be acquired by the Government of India at any time. 
 
 
 
• Article 1 of the Indian constitution:
 
 
• India, that is Bharat, shall be a Union of States.
 
 
 
• The names of states and union territories and their territorial extent are mentioned in the first schedule of the Constitution.
 
• The first Schedule contains:
 
 
• Names of the States and their territorial jurisdiction.
 
• Names of the Union Territories and their extent.
 
 
 
• Notably, the ‘Territory of India’ is a wider expression than the ‘Union of India’ because the latter includes only states while the former includes not only the states but also union territories and territories that may be acquired by the Government of India at any future time.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• ** Article 2 of the Indian Constitution** deals with the admission or** establishment of new states in the Union of India**.

 
 
• It provides for the power of the** Parliament to admit new states, or to establish new states by separating territory from any existing state or by merging two or more states or parts of states.**
 
 
 
• **Article 10** of the Constitution deals with the power of the Parliament to make laws with respect to the **reorganization of states**.
 
 
• It provides that Parliament may by** law admit new states into the Union, or establish new states by separating territory from any existing state or by merging two or more states or parts of states.**
 
 
 
• ** Article 11** of the Constitution provides for the power of the President to make certain modifications to the boundaries of states,** subject to certain conditions and procedures.**
 
 
• It states that the** President may by order, after consultation with the Governor of the state concerned, make certain changes to the boundaries of any state or alter the name, area or boundaries of any Union territory.**

questions.question: 'Mahamastakabhishek' is a ______ festival celebrated every twelve years.
questions.solution:

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

 
• ** Mahamastakabhishek is a major festival of Jains that is celebrated once in every twelve years.**

 
 
• This festival is celebrated to mark the consecration of the statue of Lord Bahubali, who was the son of the first Tirthankara, Rishabhdev. 
 
• The festival is celebrated with great enthusiasm and devotion by Jains all over the world.
 
 
 
• Sikh: Sikhism does not celebrate Mahamastakabhishek as it is a festival of Jainism.
 
• Buddhist: Buddhism also does not celebrate this festival as it is specific to Jainism.
 
• Hindu: Although Hindus have many festivals, Mahamastakabhishek is not a Hindu festival but a Jain one.

questions.question: Which of the following is a symptom of bacterial infection?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** fever.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• ** Fever is a common symptom of bacterial infection as the body's immune system responds to the presence of bacteria by raising the internal temperature.**
 
• ** Other symptoms of bacterial infection may include fatigue, muscle aches, and chills.**
 
• Bacterial infections can be** treated with antibiotics,** but it is important to identify the specific bacteria causing the infection to ensure the right medication is prescribed.
 
• If left untreated, bacterial infections can lead to more serious complications such as sepsis or organ failure.
 
• Bacteria that can cause disease are known as pathogenic bacteria.
 
• Pathogens can spread through the air, skin contact, bodily fluids, etc.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Cardiac arrest, fracture, and heart attack are not symptoms of bacterial infection. Cardiac arrest is a sudden loss of heart function, while a fracture is a break in a bone and a heart attack occurs when blood flow to the heart is blocked, typically due to a buildup of plaque in the arteries.
 
• However, bacterial infections can sometimes lead to complications that affect the heart or other organs.
 
• For example, untreated streptococcal infections can cause rheumatic fever, which can damage the heart valves.
 
• It is important to seek medical attention if you suspect you have a bacterial infection, as prompt treatment can prevent serious complications.
